jun: heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selector tweak i'm seeing a small but consistent p99 regression on m7b/8x7b streaming traces. attaching notes.

sarah: ok, what workload? nightly or ad-hoc?

jun: streaming long-context sim (overlap sliding-window, seq ~2k). p50 flat, p99 ~+15% on token latency. GPU util not spiking, but we see extra kernel fallbacks during KV reuse.

ben: can you paste profiler snippet?

jun: sure — gist of logs:
```
[kernel-selector] chosen=matmul_opt_v2
[kernel-fallback] chosen=matmul_generic reason=kv_align_mismatch tokens=1024-1030
[kv] reuse: cached_max_pos=4096 runtime_max_pos=2048 -> kv_align_mismatch=true
```
This pattern shows up whenever the request stream reuses a cached KV buffer that was allocated with a different max_pos.

oliver: kv_align_mismatch sounds like the allocator alignment change we landed last week. that could change tiling/packing assumptions and trigger a generic path.

jun: exactly. fallback means we re-run a slower matmul path and also touch the KV buffers differently which leads to extra memcpy and mask recompute. appears tied to rope scaling path selection too.

maria: that would also explain the attention-mask off-by-one weirdness we saw in a few evals. if the kernel expects rope scaled to N but buffer was to M, mask boundaries shift slightly during the fallback window.

sarah: do we have a minimal repro?

jun: yes — small script that streams two overlapping windows and reuses the same cache handle. i'll paste later. repro shows deterministic p99 bump in ~200 samples.

ben: short-term mitigation?

jun: proposal: implement "sticky kernel" heuristic for streaming KV reuse — pin the selected kernel for a small duration (e.g., sticky_kernel_duration=2s) per stream handle so transient selector oscillation doesn't cause fallback thrash. also emit metric counter kernel_fallback_reason=kv_align_mismatch.

perf-bot: perf-bot: regression alert — nightly/m7b/streaming p99 increased +15% between commits abc123 -> def456. report: /perf/report/2103

oliver: long-term we should make kernel selection consider cached_max_pos/runtime_max_pos equality as a hard constraint rather than fallbackable condition. i.e., if mismatch -> prefer no-switch or safe-copy fallback that preserves mask semantics.

maria: agree. i'll add evaluation prompts to catch mask border cases after kernel switches so we don't regress silently.

sarah: nit: be careful not to over-pin kernels for models that intentionally switch kernels (eg qwen/mixtral where head dims differ). sticky should be per-model-tag and opt-out for known multi-kernel models.

jun: plan of attack: 1) add metrics + logging for kernel selection reasons 2) quick sticky-kernel pin by stream handle 3) add assertion check in reuse path (runtime_max_pos==cached_max_pos) gated behind a flag 4) run targeted e2e with sliding-window evals 5) rollback knob if canary shows other regressions.

ben: :thumbsup: on metrics first.

oliver: also add trace id to every fallback log line so we can join with token-level traces.

jun: opening issue/PR now, will include repro, perf snippets, and a conservative sticky implementation. link: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-4123

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for next canary window — team watch please.

jun: tagging @sarah @ben @oliver for review. quick check — any objections to sticky_kernel_duration=2000ms default?

sarah: nope, fine as a conservative default.

ben: fine. will watch perf dashboards.

maria: i'll add regression evals to catch mask off-by-one.

jun: thanks — i'll post PR and update the thread with perf diffs after canary. :thumbsup:
